summary: Cold read of the recorded assistant-exploration-api contract and task plan (Codex gpt-5.6-terra @ xhigh, read-only) returned NOT CONVERGED with six findings. All six were verified against the repository before being acted on and all six held, though one carried an overstatement that was dropped: the read claimed decision 0019 requires pagination for fresh routes, and 0019's text contains no pagination requirement. A seventh correction came from the orchestrator's own verification rather than the cold read - the contract sent an APP-DB migration proof to test:warehouse-proof, which is the separate WAREHOUSE_PG_* group gated on WAREHOUSE_DB_TEST=1. One finding needed the human: the approved story plan says five tables where the task builds two, and approved_plan_sha256 locks the plan body. write_scope rose from 17 paths to 27, required leaves from 6 to 7, and the review budget from 17/2200 to 27/2900.

criteria_map.A DELIBERATELY SCOPED migration creates: The hand-scoped migration. The cold read found the approved story plan says FIVE tables at plans/active/assistant-assistant-exploration.md:111 and :263 while this task builds TWO - a contradiction between a plan and the task it authorizes. approved_plan_sha256 locks the plan body, so the human chose to leave it unedited and record the supersession here. The criterion also now pins the SQL to schema.ts:254-278's exact names and corrects the casing authority: that snake_case is decision 0012's vendored app-DB convention, NOT decision 0015, whose deviation is warehouse-only (0015:17). 0015's surviving half - explicit FK indexes and timezone-aware timestamps - is now required.
criteria_map.The saved and pins modules are REGISTERE: Registration and governance. The cold read found the contract claimed decision 0019 while ignoring the half 0019 does NOT deviate from. These routes enter the public API surface for the first time, so named typed request/response DTOs, documented Swagger responses including typed 400/401/403, strict unknown-field rejection and 07-exception-handling's failure model now bind them. The cold read also asserted 0019 requires pagination; it does not - 0019's text says nothing about pagination - so that half of the finding was dropped rather than propagated.
criteria_map.The snapshot machinery is DELETED, not m: The deletion, which the original scope made impossible. The cold read found PinRefreshService is imported, provided AND exported by backend/src/core/core.module.ts at :28/:57/:75, a file that was not in write_scope: deleting the service without it fails the build, and leaving it keeps the interval live. core.module.ts is now in scope with all three references named. Pin.snapshot and Pin.lastRefresh also leave contract/src/api.ts - an optional field that is never populated is the same compatibility leftover this task exists to remove.
criteria_map.Every read re-authorizes as the CURRENT: Re-authorization, and the refusal that had no shape. The cold read found SavedQuery (contract/src/api.ts:372) and Pin (:386) each REQUIRE a runnable Selection, with contract/src/api.ts out of scope - so the criterion demanded a refusal the contract could not express. Both interfaces now gain a REQUIRED discriminated status, following the precedent at contract/src/api.ts:486, with the stored selection retained so a reader can still see and delete what they saved. Nothing in frontend/ reads either type yet, so the shape is settled before task 4 depends on it.
criteria_map.Authorization and audit are per-request: Audit coverage, under-specified and unprovable as written. The cold read found the criterion named one leaf while eight routes mutate or read, omitting PATCH /api/pins/:id/view (pins.controller.ts:69) entirely - and that RequireAction throws from INSIDE the guard (auth.guard.ts:77-90) before any controller method runs, so a denied save or pin could not be audited by any in-controller record. A route-scoped audit exception filter now catches those, modelled on MisDrillAuditFilter (mis-drill.audit.filter.ts, @UseFilters at mis-drill.controller.ts:32) under decision 0025. AuditService gains typed exploration events; event_type is free text at 0000_auth_audit.sql:80, so no migration is needed for them.
criteria_map.The behaviour is proven by hermetic leav: The proof, which could not execute. The cold read found migrate.trim.test.ts:6 pins an EXACT table list that 0001 breaks, with the file out of scope and D-0006 ignored; it is now in scope and its EXPECTED_TABLES grows by exactly two, which makes it the hermetic proof of the scope. The gated proof's home was also wrong: test:warehouse-proof is the WAREHOUSE_PG_* group behind WAREHOUSE_DB_TEST=1, so an APP-DB migration test belongs in quality-gate.test.mjs's dbTests and backend/package.json test:db beside migrate.test.ts, run against an isolated scratch database. The partition assertion at quality-gate.test.mjs:331 and the D-0006 discharge for all five ignored files this task edits are now stated.

current_flow: Task 1 registered and governed POST /api/chat and /api/chat/stream; task 2 shipped the docked Ask panel and the standalone Ask page. Saved selections and pins are vendored but INERT: app.module.ts imports neither module, app.routes.test.ts lists no /api/saved or /api/pins route, and the two tables they need do not exist - backend/drizzle holds only 0000_auth_audit.sql while schema.ts declares seven absent tables. Meanwhile PinRefreshService is fully wired into CoreModule (:28/:57/:75) with an OnModuleInit interval that would begin writing pin_snapshots the moment those tables appeared - which decision 0028 forbids. So the story's persistence layer is simultaneously unreachable and, once reachable, wrong.
new_abstractions: The first hand-written migration in the project: every prior schema change came from drizzle generation, and this one must deliberately create two of the seven tables schema.ts declares.

A route-scoped audit exception filter for saved and pins, generalising the drill's MisDrillAuditFilter so that denials raised inside a guard - which no controller method can observe - still reach the audit log.
A required discriminated runnable/refusal status on two shared contract interfaces: the first time a persisted artifact in this system can report that it has stopped being answerable.
gaps: The deletion the task exists to perform was impossible within its own write_scope: PinRefreshService is imported, provided and exported by backend/src/core/core.module.ts at :28, :57 and :75, and that file was not in scope - so deleting the service fails the build and retaining it keeps the OnModuleInit interval alive.
Re-authorization refusals had no expressible response shape: contract/src/api.ts:372 SavedQuery and :386 Pin each require a runnable Selection, and contract/src/api.ts was out of write_scope.

Audit coverage named a single leaf while eight routes mutate or read, omitting PATCH /api/pins/:id/view (pins.controller.ts:69); and RequireAction denials are thrown inside the guard (auth.guard.ts:77-90) before any controller method runs, so the promised audit of refusals could not fire at all.

The migration proof could not execute: backend/src/db/migrate.trim.test.ts:6 pins an exact expected-table list that 0001 necessarily breaks, and the file was out of scope with deferral D-0006 unaddressed.

Deviations were misapplied: the task plan attested decision 0015 for snake_case, but 0015:17 scopes that deviation to the WAREHOUSE schema and explicitly keeps the app OLTP on the constitution's casing; and decision 0019's non-deviated half - typed DTOs, documented 400/401/403, strict unknown-field rejection - was not bound to routes that become public API here for the first time.
contradictions: The approved story plan contradicts the task it authorizes: plans/active/assistant-assistant-exploration.md:111 and :263 both say the migration creates FIVE declared-but-absent tables, while the task correctly creates TWO - the difference being decision 0028's prohibition on pin_snapshots and the plan grill's deferral of durable history.

The required test for the migration proof was routed to backend/package.json test:warehouse-proof, which is the WAREHOUSE_PG_* database group gated on WAREHOUSE_DB_TEST=1 - a gate an app-DB migration test does not use and a group it does not belong to. Found by the orchestrator while verifying the cold read's fifth finding, not by the cold read itself.

The cold read's claim that 0019 also requires PAGINATION was checked and is false - the word does not appear in the decision - so it was not propagated into the contract.

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) - the two-table scope stands and the approved plan's 'five' wording is superseded in the task contract rather than corrected in the plan, because approved_plan_sha256 locks the plan body and editing it would cost a second board approval. Recorded in t-aea-c1 and flagged in reviewer_focus so a reviewer reading the plan does not reject the migration.

rounds.question: The `assistant-exploration-api` grill found the approved story plan contradicts the task it authorizes. `plans/active/assistant-assistant-exploration.md:111` and `:263` both say the migration creates the **five** declared-but-absent tables. The task builds **two** (`saved_queries`, `dashboard_pins`) — because decision 0028 forbids writing `pin_snapshots`, the plan grill deferred durable history (`conversations`, `conversation_turns`), and `authored_measures`/`reconciliation_runs` belong to features this story does not ship. The catch: `approved_plan_sha256` locks the plan body, so editing those two lines would invalidate the approval and cost a fresh board round.

Closing the `assistant-exploration-api` grill. All six findings were real and are folded in — one had an overstatement I corrected: the cold read said decision 0019 requires **pagination** for fresh routes; 0019's text says nothing about pagination, so I bound only what it actually preserves (typed DTOs, documented 400/401/403, strict unknown-field rejection). Also corrected against the repo: the migration proof was pointed at `test:warehouse-proof`, which is the separate `WAREHOUSE_PG_*` database — it moves to the app-DB group. `core.module.ts`, `contract/src/api.ts`, `migrate.trim.test.ts` and `audit.service.ts` enter write scope; the audit grows from one route to **eight** plus a guard-level filter modelled on the drill's; the refusal gains a required discriminated `status`; and the 0015 attestation is corrected — the app-DB casing is 0012's, not 0015's. Write scope 17→27 paths, required leaves 6→7. Any remaining gap before this goes to the board?
